Federico Molinari is a Canadian men’s artistic gymnast best known for being an international all‑arounder and a parallel bars specialist, and for winning one of Canada’s marquee men’s medals at the World Championships.

## Quick profile
- **Name:** Federico Molinari  
- **Country represented:** **Canada**  
- **Discipline:** Men’s Artistic Gymnastics (MAG)  
- **Signature events:** **All‑around** and especially **parallel bars** (his standout apparatus internationally)  
- **Era:** Mid‑2000s through the 2010s (including multiple Olympic cycles)

## What he’s best known for
### 2010 World Championships medal (parallel bars)
- Molinari won **bronze on parallel bars at the 2010 FIG World Artistic Gymnastics Championships** (Rotterdam).  
- That result is frequently cited as one of the major milestones for Canadian men’s gymnastics in the modern era, because Canada historically had far fewer men’s World Championships apparatus medals compared with the top MAG nations.

## Olympic participation (high level)
Molinari competed for Canada across multiple Olympic cycles and is widely associated with Canada’s push into more consistent men’s team and individual finals during that period.

- He is remembered as:
  - A **reliable all‑arounder** for Canada in qualification/team formats, and  
  - A gymnast capable of **making major finals** (particularly on parallel bars, and in the all‑around at times depending on the year).

*(If you want, tell me which Olympics you care about—2004/2008/2012 are the ones most commonly associated with his senior peak—and I can lay out what he did at each Games in more detail.)*

## Competitive style and strengths
- **Parallel bars:** Typically his highest-impact event internationally—strong swing, amplitude, and composition aimed at high difficulty.
- **All‑around contribution:** In team contexts, he was valued for being able to cover multiple events at a solid international level, not just one apparatus.

## Role in Canadian men’s gymnastics
During the late 2000s and early 2010s, Canada’s men’s program was building depth and international credibility. Molinari was part of the group of athletes who:
- Helped Canada stay competitive in **team qualification** at major meets, and  
- Showed that Canada could contend for **individual apparatus medals** at Worlds.

## After/alongside elite competition
Publicly, Molinari has also been associated with the broader Canadian gymnastics community beyond just his own competitive results (e.g., involvement in the sport after peak competition), though the specifics depend on the period you’re asking about.

3) a more **biographical** view (early life, clubs/coaches, training base, retirement and later work)?

If you tell me which of those you prefer, I’ll format it that way.
